theater: 伊利湖西南岸托萊多地帶

battle.name: 托萊多戰爭
battle.theater: 伊利湖西南岸托萊多地帶
battle.brief: 一八三五年，密西根準州與俄亥俄州為伊利湖西南端的托萊多地帶爭奪歸屬，四月與九月兩度動員民兵對峙，槍口相向而未真正開火。最終由美國國會於一八三六年劃界：地帶歸俄亥俄，托萊多市歸密西根。卡面長槍留在民兵操典與儀仗之中，雙方真正爭的是測量線與法理。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 「托萊多戰爭」並非外國國家之間的戰爭，而是同一聯邦內兩套武裝機器之間的邊界爭端，交戰雙方是美國的一個州與一個準州。俄亥俄州一方由州長羅伯特·麥克盧卡斯主持，州議會先把伊利湖西南端、莫米河與邁阿密河之間那片狹長地帶寫進州界，州長隨即援引民兵法召集本州民兵進駐爭議區；這些連隊多由西北各縣的自願農夫與城鎮工匠組成，裝備美國制式燧發滑膛槍、老式步槍與少量長矛。密西根準州一方由準州州長史蒂文·梅森主持，這位以二十餘歲之齡當選、被後世稱為「少年州長」的人物，說服準州議會正式聲索地帶，並組織準州民兵集結於底特律與莫米河下游，準備向托萊多挺進。聯邦政府由總統傑斐遜與陸軍部長劉易斯·卡斯主持，因事涉兩州主權而刻意不偏袒任何一方，最終以駐紮在舊西北地區的聯邦軍隊充當兩軍之間的緩衝。整場衝突沒有外國勢力介入，沒有正式宣戰，也沒有議定條約，全部過程發生在美國本土的行軍道路上與報紙版面上。
countriesEn: The Toledo War was not a war between foreign states but a boundary dispute fought with the military machinery of one federation against itself, and the belligerents were a state and a territory of the same republic. On the Ohio side, Governor Robert M. Lucas presided over a legislature that had already written the wedge of ground at the western end of Lake Erie, between the Maumee River and the Miami River, into the state boundary; the governor then invoked the militia law and called out the Ohio militia to occupy the disputed strip. Those companies were drawn largely from volunteer farmers and town artisans of the north-western counties and carried regulation flintlock muskets, older smoothbores and a few pikes. On the Michigan side, Territorial Governor Stevens T. Mason, elected in his twenties and known afterwards as the Boy Governor, talked the territorial council into asserting the claim in formal terms, organised the Territorial militia, and assembled its companies below Detroit and along the lower Maumee in preparation for a march on Toledo. The federal government, headed by President Andrew Jackson with Lewis Cass as Secretary of War, deliberately declined to favour either side in what was formally a question of sovereignty, and relied instead on federal troops stationed in the Old Northwest as a buffer between the two levies. No foreign power intervened, no declaration of war was made and no treaty concluded; the whole affair unfolded on American roads and in American newspapers.
people: 主要人物分屬三方。密西根準州州長史蒂文·提莫西·梅森是爭議最有力的鼓吹者，1834年他以二十四歲之齡當選準州州長，1835年兩度召集民兵，企圖用既成事實把托萊多變成準州實際上的門戶。俄亥俄州州長羅伯特·麥克盧卡斯是直接對手，他主張以1787年的聯邦測量線為界，並調動本州民兵進駐爭議地帶；兩位州長的私人對立，把一條測量線變成了兩州政治立場的試金石。民兵層面，密西根的民兵連隊由準州民兵指揮官培根率領，據編年記載曾在莫米河下游列陣；聯邦方面則由陸軍少將溫菲爾德·斯科特兩度親赴現場，命令進駐爭議區的俄亥俄民兵撤出，並接管聯邦所有堡壘，務求不讓任何一方搶先開火。國會裡，密西根準州代表索倫·博蘭為準州辯護，俄亥俄州的傑里邁亞·莫羅與約瑟夫·萬斯等人組織「反欺詐」陣線，堅持州界必須以聯邦測量線劃定，並指控另一條線出自人為做手腳。東岸報章的追蹤與全國性的選舉語言，使這場邊界糾紛在變成戰事之前，已經先變成了公共輿論的戰場。
peopleEn: The principal figures came from three directions. Stevens T. Mason, governor of the Michigan Territory, was the most zealous advocate of the claim: elected in 1834 at the age of twenty-four, he called out the militia twice in 1835 and tried to convert the physical presence of armed men into a fait accompli, making Toledo in practice the gateway of the Territory. Governor Robert M. Lucas of Ohio was his direct opposite; he maintained that the federal survey of 1787 was the true state line and moved the Ohio militia into the disputed ground, and the personal antagonism of the two governors turned a line on a map into a test of state honour. At the level of the companies, the Michigan militia was led by its commander Bacon, recorded in the chronicles as drawing his men up in the lower Maumee, while on the federal side General Winfield Scott came to the ground twice in person, ordered the Ohio militia out of the contested area, took over the federal forts so that neither side could take the first shot, and made it his business that nobody did. In Congress Solon Borland argued Michigan's case, while Jeremiah Morrow and Joseph Vance led the Anti-Fraud faction of Ohio, insisting that the boundary must be fixed on the federal line and alleging that the other survey had been made by hand. Newspaper attention on the eastern seaboard and the vocabulary of a national election turned the quarrel, before it became a shooting war, into a battle of public opinion.
kits: 卡面是西班牙長槍，屬於十六世紀末至十七世紀初方陣火槍組合的核心兵器：長槍手密集結在前列，火槍手退到方陣內側與後方，用來頂住衝鋒的騎兵。1835年的北美民兵操典裏，這套邏輯以另一種形式殘存：由刺刀構成的方陣，仍是受過操練的民兵面對騎兵與亂民衝撞線面時的標準應對；少數連隊甚至保留實體長矛，由指定的士兵在操練與閱兵時持舉，充當軍官儀仗與古老傳統的標誌。真正用於戰鬥的，是兩州民兵手上的滑膛燧發槍：密西根民兵多配美國1816年制式春田造燧發滑膛步槍，口徑約五點四英寸，附套筒刺刀；俄亥俄民兵除制式槍外，還有大量獵槍、私人藏存的各式舊槍與少量騎槍。砲兵方面，兩州民兵都設有砲兵分隊，配備輕型野戰砲與騎砲，主要用於儀仗與前哨警戒，在1835年的實際對峙中多數未及發砲。軍官佩馬刀與佩劍，士兵隨身帶火藥壺、通條與刺刀。整體而言，這場衝突的裝備結構是「軍用制式槍械＋大量雜式槍械＋象徵性長矛」的混合體。
kitsEn: The card shows a Spanish pike, the core weapon of the pike-and-shot formation of the late sixteenth and seventeenth centuries: pike men massed in the front rank with the musketeers withdrawn behind and inside the square, where they could receive a charge of cavalry. In the North American militia of 1835 the same logic survived in another form. The hollow square formed with bayonets fixed was still the standard answer of a drilled militia facing cavalry, or a mob running at the line, and a few companies even kept actual pikes, carried by a designated rank during drill and musters as an officer's honour guard and as a visible badge of the old tradition. What really went to the field were the flintlock smoothbore muskets in the hands of the state militias: the Michigan companies were mostly equipped with the United States Model 1816 Springfield flintlock musket of about .54 calibre with a socket bayonet, while the Ohio companies added hunting guns, muskets of many private patterns drawn from private stores, and a few light cavalry carbines. On the artillery side both states kept militia artillery companies with light field pieces and horse guns, used mostly for parade and for covering picket posts; in the actual confrontations of 1835 little or no artillery was fired. Officers carried sabres and swords, and the rank and file carried powder horns, ramrods and bayonets. In sum the equipment of the Toledo War is a mixture of regulation service muskets, a large quantity of miscellaneous private weapons and a purely symbolic pike.
tactics: 若說這場衝突也有戰術，那便是「不交戰」的戰術。兩州的行動邏輯是政治先於集結：州議會先投票劃界與撥款，州長再依民兵法發出召集令，各縣逐級點名編成連隊，士兵在城鎮廣場集合後開赴爭議地帶。1835年秋，密西根民兵連隊集結於底特律以南的莫米河谷，在托萊多周圍的道路與橋樑上選擇陣位；俄亥俄民兵則自西北部沿通往伊利湖沿岸的驛道南進，試圖切斷對方退往五大湖的通道。雙方都以姿態而非火力施壓：把隊伍擺在對方看得見的公路上，把砲架在能俯瞰的高點，把刺刀上肩的縱隊展示給對方看，藉此製造「開火只是時間問題」的印象，反而消除了開火的需要。聯邦部隊的部署同樣是一種戰術：斯科特把聯邦軍隊駐紮在兩軍之間並命令雙方後退，把爭議從野地推入議會大廳。底層的風險則在武器本身：燧發滑膛槍的有效射程、裝填速度與指揮官的射擊紀律，使任何一次誤判，都足以在幾分鐘內把一場紙上戰爭變成真實交火。
tacticsEn: If the Toledo War had tactics, they were the tactics of not fighting. The logic of both states was political before it was military: the legislature voted the boundary and the money, the governor issued the call under the militia law, the counties mustered their companies by name, and the men paraded in the town squares before setting out for the disputed ground. In the autumn of 1835 the Michigan companies assembled in the Maumee valley south of Detroit and chose positions on the roads and bridges around Toledo, while Ohio columns came south from the north-west along the old lake road in the hope of cutting the other side off from the Great Lakes. Both armies applied pressure with appearance rather than with fire: they posted their men on roads the other side could see, unlimbered guns on rising ground, and marched past in column with bayonets at the charge, producing the impression that a shot was only a matter of time and so removing the need to fire one. The deployment of the federal troops was itself a manoeuvre, for Scott quartered them between the two levies and ordered both back, pushing the dispute out of the field and into the chamber. The underlying risk lay in the weapons themselves: the effective range, the loading time of the flintlock smoothbore and the firing discipline of the commanders meant that a single misjudgement could turn a paper war into real exchange of fire within minutes.
data: 能夠確定的數字不多，但幾個節點清楚。爭議地帶位於伊利湖西南端，寬處逾十英里、窄處不足十英里，面積一般史料記作約四百六十餘平方英里，涵蓋今俄亥俄州西北端的托萊多市及其周邊。測量線的關鍵年份是1787年（聯邦測量，即後來所稱的哈里斯線）、1812年（弗羅斯特線）與1816年（弗羅斯特—傑克遜線），三線在莫米河與邁阿密河之間拉出重疊，差距只有數英里。時間軸上，1835年3月兩州議會各自表態，4月起俄亥俄民兵進駐爭議區、密西根民兵亦向莫米河下游集結，7月斯科特抵達並令進駐一方撤出，9月雙方再度動員，1836年6月國會完成劃界。規模上，兩州動員的民兵以千計，但真正進入接觸線的連隊有限，多數時間耗在行軍與駐紮。按當時驛道里程概算，托萊多至底特律約三百公里，至克利夫蘭約一百五十至兩百公里，這段距離決定後勤只能靠車隊與當地徵糧維持。交火極少，主流記述是沒有發生決定性的射擊。
dataEn: Few figures can be fixed, but several landmarks are solid. The disputed ground lay at the western end of Lake Erie, more than ten miles wide in places and less than ten in others, covering an area that standard accounts put at rather more than four hundred and sixty square miles, and it included the city of Toledo and its surroundings in the north-west corner of Ohio. The decisive survey years were 1787, when the federal line, later called the Harris line, was run; 1812, when Colonel Robert Frost ran his own line; and 1816, when Frost and Jackson surveyed again. The three lines overlapped over a belt of only a few miles between the Maumee and the Miami. The chronology runs as follows: in March 1835 both legislatures stated their claims; from April the Ohio militia entered the strip while Michigan companies assembled in the lower Maumee; in July Scott arrived and ordered the occupiers to withdraw; in September both sides mobilised again; and in June 1836 Congress completed the settlement. In scale the levies on both sides ran into the thousands, but the number of companies actually brought to the contact line was small and much of the time went into marching and garrison duty. Judged by the stage road distances then in use, Toledo lay about three hundred kilometres from Detroit and between one hundred and fifty and two hundred kilometres from Cleveland, and those distances forced the commissariat to work by wagon and by local requisition. Firing was extremely rare, and the standard account is that no decisive exchange of shots took place.
cause: 起因可分三層。第一層是測量與特許：1787年英國歸還西北領土時，聯邦依《1787年條例》自密西根湖南端正北劃界，這條線後來被稱為哈里斯線，構成俄亥俄的依據；1812年與1816年密西根方面的測量則把同一片土地劃入準州。兩套測量在地面上的差距只有數英里，而量錯與故意做手腳在現場看起來一模一樣，這宗公案因此無法靠「看看地」來了結。第二層是政治與經濟：俄亥俄1803年入州，密西根1805年設準州，兩地同時面臨拓殖、運河與港口的競爭，托萊多港與邁阿密—莫米運河的未來，使這塊向來邊緣的地帶忽然變得昂貴。第三層是選舉與黨派：梅森需要一場「守土」的政治勝利，俄亥俄的「反欺詐派」則把測量線當作州格與州權的問題，兩州議員在國會互相指控，第二陣線不時延伸到自由州與蓄奴州在聯邦的票數交換上。
causeEn: The causes ran in three layers. The first was survey and charter. When the British returned the north-western territory in 1787, the federal government ran a line due north from the southern end of Lake Michigan under the Ordinance of 1787; that line, later called the Harris line, is the basis of the Ohio claim, while the surveys of 1812 and 1816 carried out for Michigan put the same ground inside the Territory. The two lines differed by only a few miles on the ground, and a surveying error and a deliberate fraud look exactly the same to a man standing on it, so the case could never be settled by going out and looking at the land. The second layer was political and economic. Ohio had been a state since 1803 and Michigan a territory since 1805, and both were competing for settlement, for canals and for ports; the future of the port of Toledo and of the Miami and Maumee canals made a piece of land that had always been marginal suddenly expensive. The third layer was electoral and partisan. Mason needed a patriotic victory to defend the standing of his territory, the Anti-Fraud party in Ohio made the survey line a question of state character and state right, and in Congress the two delegations traded accusations, with the balance of free and slave states in the Union never far below the surface.
impact: 影響主要落在制度與地緣兩方面。其一，國會被確立為州界爭端的最終裁判者：1836年6月的劃界立法把大片地帶判給俄亥俄，把托萊多市連同其周圍數平方英里判給密西根；密西根隨即依這條線起草1836年州憲法，並於1837年1月加入聯邦，成為美國第二十六州，托萊多遂成為新州的門戶與最大城市，至今仍是俄亥俄州西北部的工業與運輸樞紐。其二，那條被當事人指為「欺詐線」的測量線此後長期是未決的怨憤：地帶居民與兩州政府曾為此反覆提起訴訟，直到二十世紀七十年代，兩州才以州際協議把這條線正式勘定測量。其三，1835年秋天這場隔著射線對峙而無人願先動手的案例，成為美國政治史上少數可用來說明聯邦常備軍仲裁角色的樣本，也說明民兵制度的雙面性：它可以是國家擴張的階梯，也可能在聯邦介入之前，把國家拖向內戰式的分裂。
impactEn: The consequences fell on institutions and on geography. First, Congress was confirmed as the final arbiter of interstate boundaries: the legislation of June 1836 awarded the bulk of the strip to Ohio and the city of Toledo with a few square miles around it to Michigan; Michigan then drew up its state constitution of 1836 on that line and entered the Union in January 1837 as the twenty-sixth state, Toledo becoming the new state's gateway and largest city and remaining today the industrial and transport hinge of north-western Ohio. Second, the survey line that the contestants themselves called fraudulent stayed an open grievance for generations: the men of the strip and both state governments brought suits over it repeatedly, and it was not until a compact between the two states in the 1970s that the line was formally surveyed and fixed. Third, the standoff of September 1835, in which two militia forces faced one another down a line of sight and nobody would move first, became one of the few cases in American political history used to illustrate the arbitral role of the federal army, and equally the double nature of the militia system, which can serve as a ladder for national expansion and can, in the hour before federal intervention arrives, drag the country towards something like civil war.
result: 結果分軍事的與政治的兩層。軍事上，1835年9月第二輪動員之後，兩軍在莫米河一線再度僵持，最終在聯邦部隊與聯邦當局斡旋下各自撤回原駐地，沒有任何一役被判為勝負，雙方也拿不出可以宣稱的戰果，爭議地帶在多數時間裡維持實際控制的模糊狀態。政治上，1836年6月國會以立法解決：托萊多市及其附屬土地歸密西根準州，爭議地帶其餘部分歸俄亥俄州；密西根隨後依此劃界制定州憲法，1837年1月26日獲准加入聯邦。原本以「開火」為籌碼的僵局，最後以測量、辯論與表決收場；托萊多戰爭留下的教訓是，民兵動員可以是政治姿態，但州界真正的憑證始終是法律與測量，而不是槍口。
resultEn: The outcome had a military half and a political half. Militarily, after the second mobilisation of September 1835 the two forces stalemated once more along the Maumee and then withdrew to their own districts under the mediation of the federal troops and the federal government; no engagement was adjudicated a victory, neither side could point to a result worth naming, and the effective control of the disputed ground stayed undefined for most of the period. Politically, Congress settled the matter by statute in June 1836: the city of Toledo and the lands dependent on it went to the Michigan Territory and the rest of the strip to the State of Ohio; Michigan framed its constitution on that boundary and was admitted to the Union on 26 January 1837. A standoff that had been held together by the threat of a shot ended instead with survey, debate and a vote. The lesson of the Toledo War is that a militia muster may be a political gesture, while the true evidence of a state boundary is law and measurement, and never the muzzle of a gun.
